about: Hand-kept map of the design. Edit this file, then run npm run overview. Issue titles and states come from docs/overview-issues.json, refreshed with npm run overview:refresh (needs gh). npm run overview:check fails if a note, heading, area or issue reference is wrong, or if overview.html is stale.

areas.name: Farming and the day
areas.builtNote: Farming, energy, clock, sleep and save work in the browser.
areas.summary: Plant, tend, harvest and sell inside a day with an energy budget and a clock.

items.t: Energy plus a running clock; passing out is a small cost, never a lose state
Numbers are placeholders listed in one note
Tuning needs more playtests
A shipping bin is added; it pays at sleep at the shop price
Bin menu is the inventory grid (tap or drag ships the whole stack, a quantity prompt ships singles) with a Shipped today tab for take-back; collection page in M3; extra bins in M5; no bin-only items
The bin stands beside the house door; sleeping shows a shipping summary screen (items, money, total) before the morning report
Farm growth tools: three sprinkler tiers with add-ons, fruit trees, two fertilizer tiers, greenhouse and farm cave; no crows

Farm tool, tree and machine numbers are Stardew's: fertilizer in the shop, sapling prices, 25,000g cave mark, machine times in Stardew minutes; sprinkler add-ons are a Ring 2 item from the warden head
Farm types: Standard and Woodland first, Meadow starts with a coop and two chickens, locked choice on the new game screen

areas.name: Seasons, weather, foraging
areas.builtNote: Four seasons, weather and the forecast, forage and crops for every season, and the area forage tables are built. Storm strikes are not (slice 3).
areas.summary: What grows and what can be found changes with the season.

items.t: First playable has two seasons
Autumn and winter crops and forage

areas.name: Skills, tools and quality
areas.builtNote: Skills, professions, tool upgrades, quality tiers and eating are built (#60).

items.t: Tool upgrades, skill perks and quality tiers

Axe, pickaxe, hoe and can share one ladder: five grades, gold plus 5 bars, a 2 day wait at the smith dwarf; copper axe clears large stumps, steel clears large logs and the Secret Woods log (Stardew's rules, answers part of #194)
Young tree and seedling swings per axe grade, large stump and log yields, smith closing on festival days
A minimum-quality rule on a bundle item is not designed

areas.name: Village hall and bundles
areas.builtNote: Nineteen of the 30 bundles work (note 07, "Village hall"): the Foragers' Shelf has four, the Larder six, the Water room six (13 to 18, 2026-11-10), the Hearth two and the Guests' Board one (the Dyer's). The Last Seat has none yet. Finishing the Water room opens the Lake cove ferry.
areas.summary: Six rooms, 30 bundles, ending at The Last Seat, the one gate to ring 2.

items.t: Six rooms, 30 bundles, rooms appear by total bundles done
The Last Seat is the single gate to ring 2
The hall is one scrolling interior: four walled rooms and two alcoves (tank, board), a scroll each; all six drawn in slice 1
The hall main room is a hub with a six-mark progress plaque over the hearth; corridors left and right, entrance bottom centre
The hall shows a room reward; each system reads Hall.completedRooms
Every item, count and reward is a placeholder
Item pools, Last Seat numbers and pacing
Does the Last Seat need a bundle from every room?
Bundle data model (the next-payoff item)
Rewards pass done: bundle 15 gives Beach warp totems, bundle 20 a small glow ring, bundle 29 a large chest; found things from surface digging and the mines
Build in five slices, one hall room each; slice 1 is year one on the farm, all four seasons
Year one's last day does not end the game and has no year-end screen; winter 28 rolls into spring of year 2, as in Stardew
Crafting follows Stardew: a pause menu tab plus a bought workbench that uses adjacent chests; fences do not decay; lamp-posts need a battery pack, made by a lightning rod in harmless storms
Fiber comes from weeds only and sap from chopping common trees and stumps, both as in Stardew; weed rate and tree growth days are placeholders

Wood comes from about 100 farm trees on a dense day 1 farm, so wood is plentiful and energy is the limit; the carpenter also sells wood; trees are chopped with an axe (Stardew's 10 swings a tree, 5 a stump, held to repeat); goods that miss a full bag lie on the ground and walk-over pickup pulls them in

Tree types by region are decided for M3, not M2: three types in fixed places outside the farm, regrowing when chopped, some cosmetic and not choppable (owner, from play); names, seeds and yields are open

Three woody obstacles, not one: the stump a chopped tree leaves is separate from the starting field's hardwood stumps and the bigger, tougher hollow logs, which need a better axe (owner confirmed; axe tier is partly answered by note 44, yields open)
Equipment as Stardew: two ring slots, boots (Defense and Immunity), hat, shirt and pants; Stardew's ring list; the slot and the glow and magnet rings are built in slice 3
The first part of the mines (floors 1 to 10, ore shop, furnace, no creatures) is built in slice 1 so bars exist for sprinklers and machines
Greenhouse arrives in slice 4 with the animal bundle, as in Stardew; bundle 20 moves to slice 4; bundle 12's pool avoids keg goods
Weaver's and Dyer's ask for raw goods (their rewards are the loom and dye vat); Fodder takes wheat as in Stardew; slice 4 stays as one room per slice
Draft item pools for slice 1 bundles and the fall and winter crop and forage names, for the owner to reshape
Storms follow Stardew: none in winter, summer 13 and 26 always stormy, strikes through the day caught by rods with Stardew's formula, one pack per hit rod; the rod has no reach
The lightning rod needs Cave Bat bat wing as in Stardew, so rods, packs and lamp-posts arrive in slice 3 and slice 1 storms are weather only

areas.name: Valley and town map
areas.builtNote: Every home valley map is built to shell level (2026-11-09): Forest, Secret Woods, River delta and Beach, Mountain, Quarry, Lake cove and Hearthwell with eleven interiors. No villagers stand in them yet (#599), and the owner has not played them.
areas.summary: Separate areas joined by exits, buildings as interiors. Nine valley areas on eight maps (the Beach shares the River delta map), one river line, ring 2 across the bridge.

items.t: Map style: separate areas, exits, interiors (ADR 0005)
Valley layout: nine areas on eight maps (Beach shares the River delta map, SC-34), river from Mountain to delta, farm with three exits

The Outpost (2026-11-06): the carrier post moves out of the general store; the hall steward is postmaster and lives at the Outpost (nobody lives at the hall); the courier hangs out there without working; it handles mail and parcels, a notice board, road news and travelling traders
Hearthwell holds all Brimmers; hall at its east end; sawmill; log gates the Secret Woods
Farm types: hand-authored maps, less farmland for a perk, two in the first version (Standard, Woodland), about six later; only the three exits are fixed

Farm layout (draft): dense day 1 clutter with no cleared plot, about 80 by 65 tiles, house north-east, bin and mailbox by the door, wake at the bed, two ponds (only the big south one holds fish), exits north Forest, east Hearthwell, south River delta, no hidden fourth exit, farm cave a small interior map

Farm layout: exact tillable count, field shape, starting clutter counts; note 19 still says one pond; the 80 by 65 size is an unchecked Stardew claim (SC-25); fixed building positions (SC-24) and clutter regrowth by season (SC-29) are answered, the regrowth amounts are open

Valley map asset (docs/valley-map.html, built from docs/valley-map.json by npm run valley-map): two views, the valley and a zoomed Hearthwell, with area names, main buildings and all 30 people as placeholder role labels; design reference only, positions are diagrammatic, and the three non-shop Hearthwell homes are enterable burrows that stand apart; update the JSON when note 19, 20 or 55 changes

The Outpost (draft): two boards (Help Wanted stays at the store, road news at the Outpost from day 1, Special Orders appear later as in Stardew, SC-32; the working Orders board is on the Outpost wall since 2026-11-10), one road trader on Wednesday and Saturday with seeded stock at 1.5 times sell value, the farmhouse TV gives the same forecast (SC-33), road news is gossip plus trader notice plus tomorrow's weather, and a channel table that gives each way of talking to the player one job

Interiors (draft): 23 interior maps in total. Coop and barn are walked into and, like the farmhouse, each is one map that grows with its tier, unbuilt space black void (note 68, SC-36); the greenhouse is walked into; everyone outside Hearthwell with a shop or home gets one map (hermit's tower, farmstead, forge, fisher, Beach elf); the Outpost has two maps; the stonekeeper, trainer and Wanderer have none; the farmstead has visual-only paddocks outside; Stardew footprints coop 6x3, barn 7x4, greenhouse plot 12x10, interior sizes measured from screenshots, coop 11x8, 15x8, 22x8 and barn 17x13, 21x13, 24x13 (SC-38)

Growing interiors (draft): farmhouse, coop and barn are each one map holding every tier, the start room never moves, unbuilt space is black void, the camera is clamped to the built rooms, an upgrade lands overnight, the coop door stays bottom left and the barn door moves by tier; storage in Stardew is not checked, so the rules are stated as what the player sees (SC-36)
Water room ferry route; confirming the area sizes against the first Tiled drafts

Area sizes (draft): Hearthwell 120 by 110 and Forest 120 by 120 match Stardew's totals (owner), Farm 80 by 65, Mountain 80 by 70, Secret Woods 48 by 40, delta with Beach 100 by 70, Lake cove 50 by 40, Mines floor 60 by 40; the last three are our guesses (SC-40)

Special Orders (draft): board opens Fall 2 of year one as Stardew, clock starts on acceptance (ours), first completion pays a unique reward and repeats pay gold; farm debris (rocks, twigs) returns in small capped amounts each season except winter (note 65, SC-32, SC-29)

View size: default 30 by 17 tiles (about 510), wider or squarer windows show more, player zoom setting plus pinch with a cap each way (75 to 200 percent, as Stardew), HUD anchors to the edges, maps need border margins (ADR 0009, SC-42). Build plan: no cap on the extra view, menus keep a centred 960 by 540 box, separate UI size setting, 75 to 150 percent, black bars around small maps (note 64, SC-46, SC-63)

A stable and a horse as in Stardew: one per player, 10,000g plus Hardwood and iron, speed 6.6 against running at 5, outdoors only, no feeding; extras carrot, book, flute, hats. Walk speed stays at 5 tiles a second as an assumption (SC-41)

Map areas design pass (draft, 2026-11-08): one note per unbuilt area, Forest 120 by 120, Secret Woods 48 by 40, Mountain 80 by 70, River delta with the Beach 100 by 70, Lake cove 50 by 40 and Hearthwell 120 by 110, each with a tile sketch, exits and entries, resources, forage, fishing, people, contract needs and slices; build order Forest, Secret Woods, delta, Mountain, Quarry, Forest part 2, cove, Hearthwell shell, Hearthwell interiors, Beach elf. The owner answered all eleven questions on 2026-11-08: the maps are in M3b; no Secret Woods creatures yet and no Mahogany (reopened 2026-11-10, planted only, note 36); fishable woods pond (47 fish); Beach footbridge broken until 300 wood; nobody keeps the ferry; cove gets a hidden treasure spot (drafter pick, owner may veto); Hearthwell blacksmith does upgrades and geodes, the Mountain dwarf is a Mines-side trader; Hearthwell river in two arms with the layout still to design; festivals use a decorated Hearthwell variant; the horse rides every outdoor valley map; the stonekeeper gets a Quarry

River delta with the Beach (steps 1 to 4 built 2026-11-09): the 100 by 70 map with marsh lake, river channels and sea, the farm's south exit, the fisher's hut with the rods, bait and lures moved out of the general store, the marsh and Beach forage tables and tide pools, and the tide pool footbridge mended with 300 wood; the Hearthwell exit is not built (the ferry, pots and the legend are built since)

Mountain (steps 1 to 3 built 2026-11-09): the 80 by 70 map with the lake and river source, pines, rocks and forage, the stone footbridge, the six lake fish, the Forest exit, and the rockfall and mine mouth that move the Mines door off the farm (open from Spring 5); the forge, the stonekeeper's yard, the Quarry exit, the Hearthwell exit and pots are not built

Ten map contract additions for the areas: water kinds, the massive log, per-map forage tables, tree kind, per-map stump regrow, conditional layers, rideable flag, cart and board service kinds, nightly spawns

Secret Woods (steps 1 to 4 built 2026-11-09): six large stumps regrow every morning for 2 Hardwood each, a steel axe clears the massive log once, and the carpenter's temporary Hardwood sale is removed in the same slice

Forest (built 2026-11-09, #637 and #638): six groves of about 150 choppable oak and maple regrowing at 20 percent a night give the steady wood supply; the keeper's farmstead north-east now sells young animals and hay (the carpenter no longer does), the hermit's tower south-west and the Wanderer's camp by the farm road are built; names, the hermit's stock and the paddock animals wait

Hearthwell (shell built 2026-11-09, #645; interiors built 2026-11-09, #646): river in two arms with the sawmill on the main one, the hall on the island and the broken bridge on the east arm; trees cosmetic; interiors by template; people with #599

Hearthwell river layout (built 2026-11-09, #661): the terrain map with the 7 wide main arm bending once east under the festival green, the 5 wide east arm, three bridges, streets and avenues, 12 reserved lots and the arms rejoining as one river out of the south edge; the shell (#645) then added the exits to the farm, Mountain and delta, the building exteriors and the hall and sawmill doors

Quarry (built 2026-11-09, #649): the 60 by 44 map past the Mountain's ravine bridge that the Foragers' Shelf mends, rocks and ore that regrow every night (7 attempts, 2 more a year, at most 16), and the stonekeeper dwarf at his camp with no trade; hard rock, ore level gates and gem nodes not built

Smith split (owner, 2026-11-08): the Hearthwell blacksmith does tool upgrades, geode cracking and ore and does not buy geodes; the Mountain smith dwarf is a Mines-side trader (lamps, rest-camp supplies, buys ore, no upgrades). Built 2026-11-10 (#708): upgrades and geode cracking at the Hearthwell smithy, which buys no geodes; the dwarf buys ore and sells coal and weapons for coin (no weapon forging until a later forge, as Stardew's Ginger Island); the forge hut has no gate; lamps not built. Since 2026-11-10 the smithy also sells and buys ore and sells coal, at the dwarf's prices

areas.name: Story, lore and ending
areas.summary: A cozy valley, a missing relative, the Dawn Carriers and a dark lord who is never seen in ring 1.

items.t: Ring 1 has no whispers of the dark lord
No lose state; tone rules
The warden head's six-stage reveal; she visits the farm after the bridge
The player's story and ending
Final game name: Elderglen (ADR 0011, register check open)

areas.name: Rings, travel, expeditions
areas.summary: Ring 1 is the home valley and Hearthwell. Ring 2 is a haven; ring 3 is late and optional.

items.t: Ring 2 opens when The Last Seat is finished
Fairy rings carry the player out from the farm; no second farm
Home base: come home each night, or outposts
Ring 2 shape and travel
What is community centre 3?

areas.name: Cast and villagers
areas.summary: About 30 named villagers in ring 1. Almost none are named.

items.t: Ring 1 cast near Stardew's size; every villager has a saved friendship
Hermit is a witch; Old Greencoat is the Wanderer; sea elf sells the pin
Ring 1 cast structure: 30 people, races, genders, households, 14 candidates
Names, ages and looks for the ring 1 cast

The hermit witch Rosmarin (named 2026-11-09): fairy rings are gold plus rare items, edged with local material; unlocked by a lost-recipe quest (gather the pieces from villagers, cook the dish for her), overgrown herb-hung tower; the four pieces are held by the inn keeper, store keeper, retired couple and hat-maker (not tied to a festival); the dish is Remembrance stew (cheese and potato, honey, a spice, a pressed flower); open: the exact spice and flower items and prices; the tower is in the Forest and her hook is keeping the old customs as a living ledger

The warden head knew Oriel; stage 1 is a hidden note trail (as Qi's), her ring 2 challenges sit on a board of her own, stage 3 gives a carrier's mark; dusty mended coat that changes over the rings (first small change at stage 3), dry brief voice, alias Lane, real name Aldreth (ADR 0013), an old ruling line that matters to the ending; the trail is four notes, the first in the Secret Woods and written to Oriel, with three drops near the village (fish, jar, crop) paying a dish, a rare seed and a rare ore; her board is a room in her ring 2 haven base, two weekly odd, big orders (Stardew-like) paid in carrier tokens, a shop of rare one-off goods, and three one-off stage 5 errands that retrace Oriel's road, ending with Oriel's own old mark

The warden head: how her old line matters to the ending (parked for ring 3, M6, after ring 2), the trail's exact items and gift values, the shop list and token prices, the board's order list, the stage 5 errands' exact stops and milestones

The sea elf is Thalwen (renamed from Ondrel, too close to Oriel): she knew Oriel only slightly, cannot say why she has not sailed home across the sea (not the ring 2 haven), wears a travelling coat and keeps a half-packed trunk, lives in a cottage on the Beach dunes; her unfinished business ties to an old friend among the ring 2 haven elves and plays as a keepsake quest like Birdie's, her voice is dreamy and courteous with slipping plans, and the pin comes from her trunk at 3 hearts

The sea elf: the haven elf's slot, the keepsake and token, whether she leaves or stays; the Homeward pin opens at 3 hearts, exact price still open (stall built #641 at a placeholder 1,500,000g, not yet gated by hearts)

Villager schedules (not built, #599): timed routes with weekday, season, rain and festival variants, seven named weekdays, shop hours with one closed day each (store, smithy, sawmill, hatter, library, healer, inn, Outpost and two area counters), the inn as the evening meeting place, short routes for children and elders, one or two weekly town trips for six area residents, a Wednesday market, closed-day outings, all 30 named with birthdays, and the reeve as Hearthwell's leader. Default and rain routes for all 30 are drafted
Villager routes: season overrides, festival spots, heart-event and spouse routes, and the closed-counters-per-weekday count; the Stardew rows SC-106, SC-108, SC-109 and SC-110 are unchecked

areas.name: Dialogue and voice
areas.summary: Authored lines in priority tiers, capped branching talks, and a voice sheet per character.

items.t: Authored lines only, no runtime generation
Base pool plus reactive layer, strict priority tiers, capped branching graphs, four release layers
A voice sheet per character before any variant lines
Condition vocabulary, heart thresholds, global flags, journal design

areas.name: Friendship and marriage
areas.summary: Friendship rides on the cast; marriage follows Stardew's shape in our own content.

items.t: Hat standing is a light cosmetic readout of friendship
Ring 1 has 14 candidates, any player can court any, no pairing limits
Flowers to court, a non-worn ring-like token to propose
Small spouse helps, gentle divorce with a fee, children by choice, no roommate
Stardew scale (250 a heart, 10 or 8 hearts), no decay, one gift a day and two a week, five taste tiers, birthdays x8, quality bonus, bad gifts cost points
Heart events are full cut-scenes, start on walking in with a warning, may reward, and can be replayed from the journal

Six named universal loves, a long universal hate list (four categories plus named items), the first eight people's draft tastes, and the Midwinter pairing (random among people met, letter on Winter 13)
Heart event scene commands and validator rules (draft)
Names for Moonwool, the Blue Ribbon Melon and the Glimmerstone, tastes for the other 22 people, heart event lists
Item forms, divorce fee, child room upgrade, ring 2 and 3 counts

areas.name: Mines and gentle combat
areas.builtNote: Built 2026-11-08: 120 floors in bands, health, three weapon families in five tiers, the trainer, twelve creatures, the Combat skill and defeat. The smith dwarf sells weapons for coin (2026-11-09). Not built: lamps, rest-camp supplies and the lightning rod (#598).
areas.summary: Opens Spring day 5, 120 floors in three bands. Combat is real-time, gentle and optional, and mining works without it.

items.t: Mines open on Spring day 5; Old Greencoat says the way is clear and gives nothing else
Real-time, forgiving combat; one health bar shown only where health can be lost; Assist toggle and a no-creatures setting
Defeat the Stardew way: carried out, 10 percent money (cap 1000g) and up to 3 bag stacks lost, one posted back by the trainer
Stardew-sized mine: 120 floors in three bands, a lift stop at every floor reached, a loot chest camp every 10th floor, a dangerous mode switch at the bottom
Three weapon families, Combat as a fifth skill, a training dummy and a trainer; no boss fights
Creatures from cozy to a little edgy: gloop, moths, crabs, beetles, bats, thieves and old miner skeletons
Any pickaxe digs any ore; the pickaxe and farm rocks from the start
The smith dwarf sells ore and coal, not bars; she gifts the furnace after the first copper ore; the Smith's bundle gives 20 coal
Fifth tool tier metal Hearthsilver, floors 100 to 120, bars only, no gold (answers part of #194)
Dry-streak odds for ladders (also on a kill) and rare finds
A Skull Cavern style dig, likely in ring 2, and the big furnace as a ring 2 reward
Smith ore at about 2.5 times a bar's value; Nabbler steals nothing; the furnace craft makes more furnaces
Dangerous mode lever on floor 120, gated by reaching 120 and an errand from the warden head
Geodes (draft): Geode, Frozen, Magma and Omni drop by depth band as Stardew does, each with its own mineral pool, Omni drawing from all; names and prices are placeholders

areas.name: Fishing and the water
areas.builtNote: Fishing slices 1 and 2 are built: 46 fish in six waters, four rods, bait, lures and the fisher's hut on the delta. Shellfish pots are built (2026-11-10). The Water room bundles 13 to 18 are built (2026-11-10). The five legends and the crown are built (2026-11-10). Not built: trash and the recycler (#596).
areas.summary: Six Water room bundles and one Last Seat bundle depend on it.

items.t: Ring 1 has a coast; the ferry opens a lake cove; three open lakes, no cove fish in bundles
A softened bar with an assist toggle; a third skill; rod, bait and lure
Own rod line, two assist levels, the Hearthwell Carp legend at dusk in rain, a fifth tool tier from a deep mine metal
46 fish, shellfish-only traps, five legends (the Hearthwell Carp first) and the Pearl Lobster
A game-wide completion tracker (Perfection-style) is wanted; every fish and legend counts toward it (designed in 39)

Achievements follow Stardew's whole list under our own names, each with a unique hat sold at the hatter and a few mail gifts; all greyed in a collections page with a few secret; the completion total waits for the Perfection page

Request board: one request a day with 2 days to finish and no penalty; delivery and gathering first; delivery pays 3x sell price (Stardew); gathering counts from acceptance; no cap, cancel in the journal; no prize tickets yet; one quest record for board, letter and hall sources

Mail: a farm mailbox with a flag (Stardew); a trigger on day N delivers on the morning of day N+1 (Stardew); opening a letter gives its attachment at once, kept if the pack is full; read letters stay in a journal Mail section (ours); each letter is sent once

Save and exit: two records, a night record written on sleep and a resume record written quietly during play and on page hide; Continue resumes the day, Restart this day loads the night record; Exit saves; daily rolls are stored so reload never rerolls (reload as undo accepted); export and import in Options; one slot
Multiplayer is milestone M4, between the vertical slice and ring 2 (old M4 and M5 become M5 and M6); a design note settles its form before any code (ADR 0007)

Multiplayer (M4): same network only, up to 8 players; the host runs the world and guests send intents; any player can host (desktop or tablet), browsers join only; host-save characters, with travelling characters a recorded later option; free cabins when started as multiplayer, bought otherwise; host picks shared or separate money; day ends when all are in bed with a timer fallback; list games on the network or type an address; the final form is a standalone desktop game
Multiplayer: can a tablet host carry 8 players (the wrapper is settled, ADR 0008)
Achievements: a library gallery for finds, a daily request board at the general store, no rival route, a hat for every achievement, and Stardew's money thresholds re-checked at tuning

Completion total: Stardew's categories minus obelisks and the gold clock, with hall bundles and gallery donations added, each ring with its own total and reward (ring 2 is the Ginger Island counterpart) plus a valley total; always visible on the collections page; 100 percent gives a final hat, a hall scene and a keepsake

Seven elderfruit (+34 max energy each) from seven ring 1 sources: the Harvest Showing counter, the floor 120 chest, a spouse at 12.5 hearts, the hermit's high-price sale, a Secret Woods spirit for the fruit of the hermit's rare seed, the fish mail, and the full gallery set

Completion tracker details: partial progress counts, the valley total is the mean of the rings that exist, the gallery takes minerals, artifacts and found things; the rare seed is the emberseed, given by the hermit at 4 hearts, growing spring to fall
Twelve slayer goals, one per creature kind, each giving a ring or a worn hat, rebuyable from the warden head; Stardew's counts by matching role (numbers are placeholders)
Ring 2's own total: a 130-item collectible at weight 25 (100 open a room) plus eight more categories; reward is a haven hat, scene and keepsake

Ring 1's finish: a short hall scene with the steward, Old Greencoat and one line per household head, villagers in their usual hats (no hat gifting, 2026-11-10), placeholder lines until the voice sheets; keepsake is a lamp that never gutters, mailed as furniture; the valley summit is designed but built with ring 2

Four rods (only the starter limits fish; rare fish need fishing level 5), three baits, six lures with a Magpie Hook treasure table and no double catch, all sold by the delta fisher (numbers are placeholders)
Legend seasons spread across the year; eight shellfish pot catches, four per water; bundle 17 rare picks confirmed
Stardew's five bar behaviours, a first catch that cannot fail, lengths and records, water plants, trash with a recycler, hidden fish, Stardew's fishing professions; fish ponds later
Pots work as in Stardew: one bait a day and 38 percent junk, so the Trapper professions apply as written
Legend times, weather and prices, and the tracker design (what counts, weights, reward)

areas.name: Processing and animals
areas.builtNote: Built 2026-11-08: coop and barn with tiers, chickens, ducks, rabbits, cow, goat, sheep, pig, incubator, hay silo, animal-goods machines and a first cooking pass (stove, eight placeholder dishes). The Forest keeper sells young animals and hay (2026-11-09). Not built: heater, animal professions, animal art, most recipes.
areas.summary: Machines, cooking, coops and bees. Needed by many bundles. Animals are designed in 23_animals.md; processing and cooking are not.

items.t: Processing machines and cooking design
Seven animals in a coop and a barn on the farm, three tiers each, built by the Hearthwell carpenter
Feed, pet, let out; products on a timer per species; sleeping outside costs mood and one day's product only
Hay from grass and a silo, no treats; coop heater keeps winter mood up; young animals bought, incubator hatches eggs
Stardew's profession tree: Rancher or Tiller at 5, Coopmaster or Shepherd and Artisan or Agriculturist at 10
Animal prices, tier costs and grow-up days are placeholders; a valley animal of our own waits for the art pass
Eleven machines, bundle gives the first then craftable; kitchen with the 10,000g house upgrade; 81 recipes across the three rings; cask later
Bundle 27 gives a crystalarium; craft ingredient stand-ins and seed maker and smoker sources to check

areas.name: Puzzles
areas.summary: Optional logic puzzles, never gating and never punishing.

items.t: Optional only, bonus rewards
Puzzle design note: where they live and what kinds

areas.name: Customisation and hats
areas.builtNote: Hats (festival and achievement), furniture, wallpaper and flooring, and the furniture catalogue are built. Clothing, tailoring and farm decoration are not.

items.t: M3 shows hats in a portrait only (replaced 2026-10-31: world sprite)
Furniture: random daily stock at the carpenter plus a catalogue after the first house upgrade, as Stardew; one catalogue per people later
The achievement list and each one's hat are in the achievements note
Hats unlock by achievement as Stardew, are sold at a hatter's shop in Hearthwell run by the Hat-maker household, show in the world sprite, and read as a standing cue with no bonus
Hat names for the achievements that need new systems, furniture pool and prices, sewing machine cost, the per-people catalogues
Three paid house tiers add rooms, and a building's footprint never changes on upgrade, for every building
Every Brimmer home is a burrow, including the player's; the burrow ban in the lore note is lifted

Tier 1 of the house is in the first playable; tiers 2 and 3 and the cellar are M3 (spouse room from tier 2, cellar on a separate level; spouse room, nursery and casks stay sealed or empty until those systems exist)

House interior is one map per tier (start, tier 1, tier 2, no sealed earth) plus a cellar map; Stardew prices kept for the first playable; catalogue after tier 1 as Stardew; sealed rooms read as waiting
House room sizes and floor plans; built with placeholders: catalogue at 200,000g and flooring and wallpaper at 200g at the carpenter (where they are sold is still open)

areas.name: Festivals and minigames
areas.builtNote: All eight festivals are built as screens (2026-11-07): Harvest Showing table and token counter, Hollow Eve maze, Frostday sights, counters. Maps built 2026-11-08 for the Harvest Showing (village green) and Hollow Eve (hedge map, odd-year maze); other festival maps, the even-year maze and villager spots wait for the village map. The farm cave is built too (note 66).
areas.summary: Two festivals a season; the Hat Parade comes first.

items.t: One festival in M3, the hat parade; the minigame is a stretch goal

Nine festivals, two a season and a three-day winter Night Market, with final names and dates (Hat Parade, Seedswap Fair, Cake Day, Lamplight Evening, Harvest Showing, Hollow Eve, Frostday, Midwinter Feast, Winter Night Market)

Fall and winter festivals and the farm cave (draft): Harvest Showing is a 9 good display scored for points, Hollow Eve a lantern maze with a prize chest, Frostday an ice sculpture day until fishing, the mushroom cave comes with a free dehydrator (a new machine)

Festival maps: the Harvest Showing uses the village green with shops locked; Hollow Eve has its own hedge map with two mazes by year, a hidden gap and a shortcut back, and villagers inside (all Stardew)
The shop stays open until a festival opens at noon, then closes for the afternoon
Prize counter, scores, touch controls
Random seasonal events with positive or neutral results

areas.name: Platform and release
areas.builtNote: Runs in the browser and as an Android app (Capacitor, ADR 0008), installed on three tablets. The real-tablet play check is not done (#523).
areas.summary: Browser and tablet; installed wrapper later.

items.t: TypeScript, Phaser, Vite, Tiled (ADR 0004)
Installed apps: Electron on desktop (bundled Chromium, Node host shared with the test host), Capacitor with a native host plugin on tablets, browser is guest only (ADR 0008)
Project licence: PolyForm Noncommercial for code, CC BY-NC 4.0 for content and art

One tabbed in-game menu on Esc or E (Stardew), tabs in Stardew order with no Wear tab (equipment sits on the Pack tab); a separate journal on J with a quest log and a hall project log; both pause the clock; Eat stays on F; Social and Map tabs are placeholders; Exit saves the day in progress and goes to the title (ours); K is dropped; the wheel scrolls open lists; Pack gets a trash can, Auto-Sort and a bundle shortcut; Page Up and Page Down switch tabs
Desktop (keyboard and mouse) and touch are separate control profiles, never mixed; every desktop key is rebindable (Stardew); an options screen on the title and in-game menu holds controls only
Desktop defaults are Stardew's keys plus click to use and act; menu keys fixed; no run key. Eat stays on F, journal on J. Open: layout labels; gamepad parked
Desktop mouse: left-click uses the tile under the cursor within 2 tiles, else turns toward it; turn on click only; red highlight for an impossible tile; wheel down is next slot
Action intent (X, right-click) opens services and picks, shakes, harvests and eats; Use swings tools and plants (Stardew); the hand tool keeps its Use pick-up

Tap-to-move: a bare-ground tap only walks, farming is on the stick scheme; an auto-picked tool stays selected (Stardew) and pulses its slot; hold follows the finger in a straight line (Stardew); seedlings pick the axe; no hint on a plot; four-way A* in core
Mouse reach (2 tiles), tap and hold numbers, order of Action on one tile
Headless playtest: a bot on src/core/ with a seeded random and a time model, personas from note 08, bundle-chain pace reported first; browser scripts stay for input, scenes and touch
Real-tablet check
